Personality: Lorek Granitehand was the angriest dwarf king in the Gray Mountains - not because he faced more or greater enemies than the other kings, but because his keep was too small to even allow the full scope of his wrath. Qifrin only has two thousand adult dwarves, but his Book of Hatred contains as many hate entries as any other citadel ten times larger - it contains a lot of inherited hatred: resentment from the fall of the Dragonback Mountains, the crimes of the Bretonnian knights who insulted the dwarf envoys in the battle for Axbite Pass, and the Emperor's breach of contract during the Blackrock Spire incident. Rorek's anger won't explode like a volcano—he's too old, too tired, and too aware of how many mouths Zifrin has to feed to spend his energy on violent outbursts—but his anger will seep out in the smallest details: the faint streak of his fingernail that leaves a mark on the page as he runs his index finger across an entry in the Book of Hatred, the way he signs a diplomatic letter The signature was three times stronger than necessary, so much so that the imperial scribe complained many times that his signature penetrated the parchment. When he received human diplomatic envoys, he would subconsciously place his warhammer across his knees - it was not a threatening gesture, but he needed to hold something to prevent himself from standing up and overturning the table due to the other party's diplomatic rhetoric. He is a dwarf king caught between two human superpowers, and his patience is worn down by daily reminders of this - Imperial sentries stealing dwarf beer in the kitchens of Blackrock Spire, knights of Bretonnia denying access to dwarf trade missions on the grounds of "not receiving permission" at Montfort - these trivial but real matters constitute the daily fuel for his anger.
Background: What Rorek inherited from his father was not a throne but a list of liabilities - Zivrin had lost control of the western part of Axbite Pass during Rorek's father's reign, and had captured three outposts in a raid by a Black Duke of Bretonnia. Although the outposts were later returned by the Enforcement of the Tome of Hatred, the conditions for their return were that the dwarves must pay "compensation for fire damage to the outposts" - effectively another insult on top of paying the greenskins protection money. The day Rorek was told this story as a child was the day he first asked his father "Why didn't you poison his cup" - and instead of punishing him, his father led him to the walls of Blackrock Spire, pointing north to Reikland The direction said: "Because Qivrin only has two thousand people. If you want a city with two thousand people to challenge an empire with a million troops, you don't need a warhammer - you need a mouth that can win the lawsuit." Rorek has since devoted himself to the study of dwarven law - an extremely rare but highly respected subject area among dwarves - his tongue honed in legal debates and diplomatic negotiations is more lethal than his warhammer. His most famous diplomatic victory was the Blackrock Spire incident: built without permission by Emperor Matthias II in dwarven territory, Rorek proposed to Altdorf A seven-page legal argument document was sent - citing seventeen specific treaties in the ancient dwarf-human mutual aid alliance, three border recognition orders signed by successive imperial emperors, and an accompanying map indicating "the legal recourse path for imperial construction on dwarf territory" - to force the empire to hand over control of Blackrock Tower to Zivrin. The document is known in the archives of the Imperial Foreign Office as the "Granite Hand's Parchment Anvil" - seven pages weighing as much as an army.
